title: The gerund: two actions at the same time

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the gerund for parallel and simultaneous actions from B1 Unit 2 (*caminaba escuchando música*). The gerund says what someone does while doing something else, or how they do it. It fits trains that carried goods and immigrants who arrived looking for work.

items.spanish: Los trenes salían llevando café a los puertos.
items.english: The trains left carrying coffee to the ports.

items.spanish: Los inmigrantes llegaban hablando otros idiomas.
items.english: The immigrants arrived speaking other languages.

items.spanish: Las noticias viajaban por el telégrafo, llegando en pocas horas.
items.english: The news travelled by telegraph, arriving in a few hours.

sections.content: The gerund (*-ando*, *-iendo*) never changes for person or number, and it is the same actor as the main verb: *los trenes salían llevando*. It shows an action at the same time, not a later one. Do not use it for a result that comes afterwards.
